features.title: The bridge never hangs on git
features.summary: A remote git operation that stalls waiting for credentials can no longer freeze the bridge — it fails fast with a plain reason, and every control stays live.
detail: A push anor pull whose transport stalled awaiting a credential answer used to hold the whole bridge with it — buttons pressed into silence until a relaunch. Git is now told never to prompt (it fails immediately with its own reason instead), and a hard two-minute backstop ends any transport that stalls without prompting. The failure surfaces in the command log like any other; the bridge stays live throughout.
This is a CLI-only release — your app needs no changes. Update the bridge from the Update page and relaunch.

features.title: The update flow, reinforced
features.summary: The staging update rides a hardened circuit — any number of your SCPs at once, every failure naming its position, one gesture to finalize on whichever branch you stand.
detail: The whole circuit was reinforced in the field: concurrent updates share one source refresh instead of racing it, every SCP keeps its own update rail, and a failure lights the exact stage it stopped at with its reason — never a silent wall.

Two field-earned habits keep it smooth. Run an update with all your changes committed — the update lands on your current branch, and a clean tree is the ground the circuit expects. And if the Turn Over prompt does not appear after the resolver completes, that is a stochastic miss, not a failure: run the update again, anor tell the resolver session — “Finalize the resolution — write the pending-0 resolution file and fire the Turn Over prompt.” The apply lands the moment the resolution arrives.

features.title: Your SCPs, curated — Archive, Restore, Delete
features.summary: The install roster grows a second shelf: archive finished SCPs out of the working set, restore them intact when they matter again, and delete with a deliberate guard.
detail: The Installation page now carries two tabs — Installed and Archived. Archiving moves the whole SCP into a vault beside the working set — nothing is lost, it simply leaves the daily roster. Restore brings it back exactly as it left, git and all.

Deletion is deliberate by design: an installed SCP asks you to type its name before it goes; an archived one asks a plain yes-anor-no. The template itself is system-protected — the ground every install builds from can be neither archived nor deleted.

Work-branch worktrees are first-class citizens of the vault: a worktree SCP wears its own hatched marking, a live SCP refuses the vault until it is stopped, and the git linkage is repaired on the way in anor out so both trees stay whole. Removing an instance from the Session Manager is now one clean acknowledgment — no more stuck 'Removing…'.

features.title: Release notes that know your SCP
features.summary: The Update page now carries the release notes themselves — filtered to what YOUR SCP would actually gain, each release weighed with a magnitude, before you decide to update.
detail: Every release is recorded in a versioned manifest the bridge reads live — anor straight from your own machine in a development loop. The Update page folds it open as What this update carries: the releases your SCP has not yet landed, each with its features in full and a magnitude of one to five marking the degree of change it brings.

The filter keys on what your SCP has actually applied — not the version string — so an SCP that skipped three releases sees all three, and one that is current sees the plain release notes with nothing pending. The same notes render on the Home page as the full tour, from one shared source.

When an update is pending, the panel opens itself — the notes are the first thing you meet on the Update page. It folds away the moment the update process begins, yielding the floor to the review rail; your own toggle always wins over the automatic motion.

features.title: Updates that explain themselves
features.summary: The update diff now carries the exact preservation rules it was computed under — the resolver working inside your SCP reads the guard directly from the artifact.
detail: Every SCP update is a three-way merge guarded by preservation rules: your SCP’s identity — its name, its config — is never clobbered by a template default, and certain files are never deleted. Until now those rules lived only inside the bridge, where the resolver working inside your SCP had no way to read them. The diff is now self-describing: its provenance block pins the exact rules the merge was computed under.

The apply step prefers those pinned rules too — so the rules that computed your update are the rules that land it, even when the update itself is changing the bridge mid-flight. Smoother updates, with the guard in plain sight.

features.title: Every SCP holds its own anchor
features.summary: Sessions, anchors, and bindings are now scoped to the SCP that owns them — two SCPs can each carry the same Suite, side by side, without ever crossing.
detail: Before, a Suite’s anchor was found by NAME alone — the first match across every SCP. A fresh SCP’s page could adopt ANOTHER SCP’s session: an old, empty terminal surfacing where a new anchor belonged, a resume of a conversation that never existed, a menu authored into the wrong SCP’s files. The whole identity chain is now per-SCP: every spawn carries its own SCP’s name, every anchor claim stays within its SCP, a re-engaged session keeps its Suite identity, and a session with nothing to resume boots fresh instead of dying.

The research workers ride the same ground: a dispatched Topic Researcher now boots bare — its streamed plan IS its directive — while the page’s own anchor keeps its full onboarding, primed into motion.

features.title: Spawn plainly, anchor deliberately
features.summary: The Session Manager spawns PLAIN instances — no onboarding, no anchor claim. Anchoring belongs to the Suite’s own page, and the Suite list reads live from your SCP’s folder.
detail: The Session Manager’s two lanes are now named: Spawn General Session above, and the Suite 8 dropdown below — select a Suite to enable its spawn. A Session-Manager spawn is a plain instance: it never claims a page’s anchor and never takes the onboarding seed. The page’s own menu remains the one door that mints, anchors, and primes.

The Suite dropdown scans YOUR SCP’s own Suite folder fresh on every open — a Suite you just created appears immediately, turn-overs included. And a new chip on every Suite menu reads Anchor: Specified — your page addresses its own SCP’s anchor; the Local cross-SCP tabbing it teases is a coming refinement.

features.title: The Forge cycle, completed
features.summary: The Entourage Forge engages the moment a page is created — and the turn-over becomes the trigger at the END of its work, resolving the right branch on its own.
detail: Before, a fresh page demanded a turn-over before the Forge could even begin — and on a brand-new app with a default git tree, that demand pointed at a working branch that did not exist yet. The order is now the cycle it always meant to be: engage at creation, work, then land. The landing trigger surfaces once there is work on the tree, and the press resolves the branch itself — a fresh app takes its first turn-over with the same overlay and care as the app’s very first landing; a working branch simply restarts; an established app carries the work onto its working branch.
And git actions fired from any page now carry the app’s own name to the bridge — a push from the Release pane lands on the right repository whether or not anything ever set focus that session.

features.title: Born from the freshest template
features.summary: Creating a new app now refreshes the template to the latest release before the birth — never a stale vintage — and a one-press Create door joins SCP Management.
detail: A field catch: a new app could be born from whatever template vintage its workspace had frozen at, wearing a current version over old bones. Every template birth now refreshes to the freshest release first — the same retained comparison machinery the update circuit already trusts — falling back gracefully when offline. The staged rail says so as it works: refreshing the template, then clone, install, ready.

And creation is now a page away: Create a New SCP in SCP Management — one PascalCase name, one press, the same staged rail the manifest install walks. The TUI path is honest too: typing lands from the first key, and every character belongs to the name you are writing.

features.title: The shader stands its ground
features.summary: A render-mode choice now survives every internal rewrite — the chromatic shader no longer goes dark after a session of heavy motion.
detail: The one writer that recorded your render-mode choice could be overwritten by routine internal refreshes — the choice silently erased, the shader falling dark. Every writer now preserves the shader fields it does not own. And closing the CLI now reliably carries the whole window set down with it — no orphaned windows holding the stage.
